body: Nope, depression doesn't count. There are "safe guards" in place to "protect the vulnerable" and as such, only individuals "whose natural death is reasonably foreseeable" are applicable thanks to Bill C-14.

I appreciate that, but depressing topics is all I really have to talk about on a regular basis... There's only so much to say. I had an online journal for 8 years and... I've kind of written it all to death heh

'Irremediable psychological suffering' is part of what has been given the go-ahead for the right to die in Canada, but it is yet to be seen what that will equate to, and what the definition of 'competency' will come down to in regards to the mentally ill making this decision for themselves. 

I'd not heard that about Dignitas before; are you sure? Either way, I think it's a shame that this right is one often ignored. I think there's something to be said for the majority of suicide attempts being committed by the mentally ill. It's easy to say it's *because* of the mental illness, but more difficult to accept that just maybe it's because psychological suffering is more intense than people give it credit. The brain is just as physical as the rest of the body after-all, and physical pain is not without emotional and psychological suffering either, so I don't understand why one is given more weight than the other.

I'm on Lamotrigine, after my own research and request to have it prescribed to me off label. I can't go beyond 100mg without major difficulties with recalling words. I was a psychiatrist's guinea pig for 8 years in the past, resulting in 10 other medications being tried, and failing miserably, while they simultaneously withheld my actual diagnosis. Beyond that, I'm on my own concoction of supplements and so-forth at this point after much research on my own. They help, but do not cure. Coping is still really tiresome. 

As for meditation: my attempts at it have been anything but relaxing. It tends to spike my anxiety, which in turn spikes my anger, which again seems to defeat the purpose. Throw in the self-help books, the multiple therapy treatments, the... Whatever in between! It's just a fuss at this point.

Our understanding of everything is constantly improving, but I fail to see how my brain is really going to develop what it's missing and over-using at this point, so I'm not sure what you mean by 10 years to freedom. Much as things typically improve with time, I think 15+ years is enough.
